Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: C now, D prior, so the market has started to pay. Not Double Overweight: the multiples that make staples defensive derate with a 5.10% ten-year, and a defensive destination four weeks into a rotation is a crowded one. The sector rows carry B on Beverages, Tobacco, Household products, Food retail and Food production. Moves to A if defensives lead for a second month with the industry's relative strength at B or better.

memo.verdict: Park on the active watchlist. Not progress to Early-Stage Assessment, and not a kill. High conviction on the no-growth leg, medium conviction overall. Direction stated explicitly in the memo as neutral, not bearish: the business is sound, the balance sheet is strong, and the earnings path is flat, which is a reason not to spend research hours rather than a reason to be short. The memo's stated reason for the verdict is that the case fails the Triaging stage test. That test asks whether the case has large amounts of positive change forces. The memo's answer is that it has large amounts of change forces in both directions, which cancel. Named bull drivers total roughly 120 basis points of operating margin, against a modelled 150 basis point automatic wage-indexation drag. Management itself scores that arithmetic by guiding FY26/27 to at least the same operating result in absolute value and in margin. Four named re-entry triggers, with the memo requiring TWO to fire together before Early-Stage Assessment is opened: (1) combined Belgian market share at or above 28.8% for two consecutive readings; (2) organic like-for-like growth sustained above 2.5% while reported growth does not exceed it by more than a point; (3) a guided or delivered operating margin above 4.7%; (4) any credible Belgian legislative proposal to equalise joint-committee wage terms or reform automatic indexation. Named kill trigger: combined share below 27.5% for two consecutive quarters with gross margin below 30.0%.
case: The memo's argument runs in six steps.

Step one: the internal change stack is genuinely dense, dated and quantified. The French integrated retail business was sold on 28 February 2026 for EUR 231m, covering 100 stores and 45 DATS 24 stations, removing what the sources call over EUR 20m of annual operating loss drag. Easy Checkout camera scanning reached its 100th store in February 2026 and targets all 273 flagship supermarkets by end-2026, recognising up to 85% of basket items and cutting scan time by 20%. Ollignies II is a EUR 51m, 22,000 square metre goods-to-person facility consolidating 15,000 items, with seventeen self-driving vehicles running at Lot and Ollignies. Seventy percent of the self-driving pallet-truck subsidiary went to KION in July 2026 with a stated EUR 20m profit impact in FY26/27 and a 30% stake retained, and KION opened an automation centre in Antwerp to industrialise the technology across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. A EUR 100m savings programme runs alongside a selective hiring freeze. A EUR 100m buyback replaced a completed EUR 50m programme. This earns Element E1 required attribute 1 core question 2 a [B].

Step two: the external change forces are uniformly adverse, which earns the corresponding core question a [D]. Statutory loosening let franchised rivals trade every Sunday, and over 80% of Delhaize franchised stores and Intermarché locations now open on Sundays. Ahold Delhaize completed converting all 128 integrated Belgian Delhaize stores to independent affiliates, buying access to joint committees up to 25% cheaper on labour. Albert Heijn has expanded to around 80 to 85 Flemish stores with annual sales above EUR 1bn and Jumbo continues an organic rollout. Aldi at roughly 11.3% share and Lidl at 7.5% to 8.8% escalated fresh promotions. Federal law banned tobacco sales in stores above 400 square metres. The memo states the genuine tailwinds fairly: Louis Delhaize exited Belgian food retail entirely, closing seven Cora hypermarkets and leaving Carrefour the sole hypermarket operator, and the food consumer-to-producer price spread normalised, lifting second-half gross margin to 30.9% from 30.1% on average Belgian food inflation near 2%.
counter_case: The memo carries the counter-case at full strength in four places and does not soften it.

First, the risks report's own recommendation, quoted verbatim in memo Section F.6 and ADOPTED without qualification. "Stage progression verdict: Colruyt should remain on hold until organic market share stabilizes and wage indexation cost pressures subside." "Hold-and-watch recommendation: the investment idea should sit on a watch list rather than progress to active position sizing." "Unfavourable risk-reward ratio: the upside potential of +3% to 15% fails to meet the 25%+ IRR requirement for concentrated long-only portfolios." "Aggregated failure probability: the cumulative likelihood of investment failure reaches ~40% due to Belgian automatic wage indexation and Sunday store competition." Note that this counter runs in the same direction as the memo's verdict: the memo does not override the risks report, it agrees with it, and says so plainly rather than manufacturing a disagreement.
triggers: Re-entry triggers, two of which must fire together. Combined Belgian market share at or above 28.8% for two consecutive readings, which is the source's own stabilisation threshold. Organic like-for-like growth sustained above 2.5% while reported growth does not exceed it by more than a point, which directly falsifies the false-friend guardrail. A guided or delivered operating margin above 4.7%, the level at which self-help visibly beats indexation rather than merely offsetting it. Any credible Belgian legislative proposal to equalise joint-committee wage terms or reform automatic indexation, which would invalidate the core bear mechanism at a stroke and which the memo names the single largest upside optionality in the case.

Kill trigger. Combined share below 27.5% for two consecutive quarters with gross margin below 30.0%, which the sources name as the point at which commercial defences have failed. A secondary re-run trigger from the risks report is a Belgian market share contraction below 28.0%, and a persistent negative producer-to-consumer price spread exceeding 300 basis points.

Five key questions for any future stage. Did organic like-for-like growth and reported growth converge in 1H26/27, or did scope again supply the difference. Is the FY26/27 consensus of EUR 3.17 earnings per share inclusive of the KION and GEOxyz gains, worth EUR 45m to EUR 50m combined, or additive to them. What did the 146 OKay Sunday openings actually deliver against ING's estimate of over EUR 100m of sales and EUR 4m to EUR 5m of operating profit, which the memo notes is roughly 1% of group operating profit. How much of the EUR 100m savings programme reached the operating line rather than being absorbed by indexation and Sunday staffing costs. Does the Belgian food producer-to-consumer price spread stay positive, given that the entire second-half gross margin recovery came from its normalisation.

Data caveats the memo flags as material for any later reader. The forward multiple of 11.2x at the 8th percentile comes from a 16 July dashboard file and implies a share price near EUR 33.4; on the 11 August price of EUR 38.24 the same 24-month-forward earnings of EUR 2.983 imply 12.8x, so the percentile label understates where the stock now trades. Net financial debt including leases of EUR 271m, lease liabilities of EUR 401.9m and net cash excluding leases of EUR 108m cannot all hold, leaving a EUR 22.9m unexplained gap. The French exit's "over EUR 20m of loss removed" and "approximately 40 basis points of margin uplift" do not reconcile on EUR 10,568m of revenue, where EUR 20m is 19 basis points. The buy-rating percentage is 40% on the dashboard against 59% Buy and 41% Hold on the change-forces source. The distribution yield is 6.3% on the 30 June basis and closer to 5.8% at the 11 August price. Family and Korys ownership is stated at 73.50%, 77.86% and more than 55% across three sources.

Two downstream actions at memo level. Investment Analyst to re-test the two reassessment criteria against the 1H26/27 interim print around mid-December 2026 and report park-or-progress in one line. Chief of Staff to schedule a quarterly market-share and inflation-spread check from September 2026, raising a card only if a trigger fires.

One process finding for the pipeline. The coverage report asserted "Above-floor reports present: none" when three above-floor families were on disk. All three were read because the folder was checked directly. A later reader should not trust that field for this ticker.
